mechanic_1: Grow: Spend 1 Light + 1 Water for +1 Population. Repeat while able, up to the maximum.
mechanic_2: Host Plant: Monarch caterpillars feed only on Milkweed. Monarch +1 Population; Milkweed -1 Population.
extra_info: Thrives in wet habitats like swamps and riverbanks where other milkweeds would rot.

mechanic_1: Grow: Spend 1 Light + 1 Water for +1 Population. Repeat while able, up to the maximum.
mechanic_2: Drought Tolerant: Not affected by drought cards.
extra_info: An attractive groundcover and a great nectar source for butterflies

mechanic_1: Grow: Spend 1 Light + 1 Water for +1 Population. Repeat while able, up to the maximum.
mechanic_2: Pollination: Bees and butterflies may visit. Both pollinator and plant gain +1 Population.
extra_info: Bloom late into fall and winter, supporting diverse pollinator populations

mechanic_1: Grow: Spend 1 Light + 1 Water for +1 Population. Repeat while able, up to the maximum.
mechanic_2: Bee Pollination: The flower shape favors bees. Both bee and plant gain +1 Population.
extra_info: This member of the bean family blooms in March.

mechanic_1: Grow: Spend 1 Light + 1 Water for +1 Population. Repeat while able, up to the maximum.
mechanic_2: Large Plant: Sunflower may hold up to 4 Population instead of the usual 3.
extra_info: The flower head and petals are actually made of many tiny flowers.

mechanic_1: Pollinate: Monarch and plant each gain +1 Population.
mechanic_2: Caterpillar Feeding: Feed on Milkweed. Monarch +1 Population; Milkweed -1 Population.
extra_info: Houston is an important stop on the Monarch's migration path.

mechanic_1: Generalist Pollinator: Visit any flowering plant in the garden. Bee and plant each gain +1 Population.
extra_info: This large bee has a smooth, shiny black abdomen.

mechanic_1: Feed: Choose a plant. Aphids +1 Population; plant -1 Population.
mechanic_2: Honeydew Mutualism: When these Aphids feed successfully, Fire Ants in the same plot also gain +1 Population.
extra_info: Those ants block other insects, but not Anoles or Wrens.

mechanic_1: Hunt: Choose an insect that is not an assassin bug. Assassin Bug +1 Population; prey -1 Population.
mechanic_2: Ant Protection: Cannot hunt Aphids protected by Red Imported Fire Ants.
extra_info: Beneficial to gardeners because they eat destructive pests like caterpillars, aphids, and leafhoppers.

mechanic_1: Consume Honeydew: Target an aphid in the garden. Wasp +1 Population; Aphid population does not change.
mechanic_2: Parasitize: If this wasp has a population of 3, place the target aphid card face down in your plot. It becomes another aphid parasitoid wasp.
extra_info: This tiny (~3mm) wasp lay its eggs inside live aphids.

mechanic_1: Honeydew Mutualism: Protect Aphids in your plot. Each time those Aphids feed successfully, Fire Ants gain +1 Population.
mechanic_2: Hunt: Take Monarchs, Carpenter Bees, Assassin Bugs, or Parasitoid Wasps. Fire Ants +1 Population; prey -1 Population.
extra_info: Ants stop Assassin Bugs and Parasitoid Wasps from hunting protected Aphids.

mechanic_1: Hunt: Target any insect or spider. Anole +1 Population; prey -1 Population.
mechanic_2: Ignore Ant Protection: Brown Anoles may hunt Aphids even when Fire Ants protect them.
extra_info: They spread easily because their tiny eggs get hidden in the soil of potted plants and shipped around the world.

mechanic_1: Hunt: Target any insect, spider, or anole. Wren +1 Population; prey -1 Population.
mechanic_2: Ignore Ant Protection: Carolina Wrens may hunt Aphids even when Fire Ants protect them.
extra_info: Wrens also eat baby frogs.

mechanic_1: Decompose: Turn 1 face-up organism in Compost face down on bottom. Give one of your plants +1 Population.
mechanic_2: Always Playable: A decomposer may enter your plot even when no food or prey is present.
extra_info: Enter with 1 Population; maximum 3. Activate once per round.

mechanic_1: Decompose: Turn 1 face-up organism in Compost face down on bottom. Give one of your plants +1 Population.
mechanic_2: Multiply: turn 1 face-up organism in Compost face down on bottom. Give this organism +1 Population.
extra_info: The illustration is a conceptual microscope view, not a photograph.

mechanic_1: Give every plant +1 Water, up to its 3-Water cap. Return any excess to the supply.
mechanic_2: Play instead of an organism. Resolve, then put this effect face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: Effect cards never score points.

mechanic_1: Remove 1 Water from every plant that has any. Return lost Water to the supply.
mechanic_2: Play instead of an organism. Resolve, then put this effect face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: Effect cards never score points.

mechanic_1: Remove 1 Water from every plant that has any. Then one of your plants with Water left gains +1 Population, up to its maximum.
mechanic_2: Play instead of an organism. Resolve, then put this effect face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: Effect cards never score points.

mechanic_1: Discard 1 organism card from your hand face up onto Compost. It can be decomposed once.
mechanic_2: Play only with an organism in hand. Put this effect face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: Face-up organism cards are the only decomposable Compost.

mechanic_1: Choose one of your plants. Hot-day evaporation does not remove Water from it until your next turn.
mechanic_2: Keep Mulch under that plant until your next turn, then put it face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: Effect cards never score points.

mechanic_1: Choose one plant you control (any demo Plant). It gains +1 Population, up to its maximum.
mechanic_2: Play instead of an organism. Resolve, then put this effect face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: Effect cards never score points.

mechanic_1: Choose one Garden Plot. Every insect there loses 1 Population. Return lost counters to the supply.
mechanic_2: Play instead of an organism. Resolve, then put this effect face down on Compost's bottom.
extra_info: At 0 Population, organism cards enter Compost face up.
